topics.title: Square numbers and the locker puzzle

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why only square numbers have an odd number of factors, using partner factors.
Recognise a square number as a number multiplied by itself and as the area of a square.

topics.title: Patterns and properties of perfect squares

concepts.learning_objective: Use the units digit to decide when a number cannot be a perfect square.
Relate the trailing zeros and the parity of a number to those of its square.

topics.title: Perfect squares, odd numbers and triangular numbers

concepts.learning_objective: Use the fact that the sum of the first n odd numbers is n squared.
Count the numbers lying between two consecutive perfect squares.
Recognise that two consecutive triangular numbers add up to a square.
State the square roots of a perfect square and find the side of a square from its area.
Use prime factorisation to test for perfect squares and find square roots.
Estimate the square root of a number lying between two perfect squares.
Recognise a perfect cube as a number multiplied by itself three times.
Evaluate statements about the units digits, parity, zeros and digit counts of cubes.
Use taxicab numbers and the odd-number pattern for cubes.

topics.title: Cube roots, successive differences and history

concepts.learning_objective: Find cube roots and make numbers perfect cubes using prime factorisation.
Compute successive differences of squares and cubes and interpret the pattern.
Recall the Babylonian and ancient Indian terms for squares, cubes and roots.
